worksheet.title: Loop a Pattern in Code
worksheet.subtitle: Ontario Math C3.1 — repeating events
worksheet.learning_goal: I can loop a small pattern of moves to make a staircase.

parts.title: Repeat a little pattern
text: A staircase is the same step over and over. Bit's step is: go across, then go up. A loop repeats that step to build the whole staircase.
Read the code — range(3) repeats the across-then-up step three times.

parts.title: Read this Python code
parts.code:
for step in range(3):
    bit.forward(30)
    bit.left(90)
    bit.forward(30)
    bit.right(90)

parts.caption: Each repeat is one step: across, then up. range(3) makes 3 steps.

parts.title: Read it
parts.prompt: How many steps does the staircase have? ______  Each step has 2 forward moves, so how many forward moves in TOTAL? ______

parts.title: Predict, then run
parts.prompt: You change range(3) to range(5). PREDICT: how many steps, and how many forward moves in total? Then run it.

parts.title: Write your own
parts.prompt: Make Bit climb a 4-step staircase. Write the range number:  for step in range(______):

parts.title: Challenge
parts.prompt: Each step goes UP 30. If Bit climbs a 4-step staircase, how high does Bit go in total? Show your thinking.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: A loop can repeat a little PATTERN of moves, not just one move. Repeat the across-then-up step and Bit builds a whole staircase.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Grade 3 · Intro Python Turtle
teacher_guide.title: Loop a Pattern in Code
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students see a for-loop repeat a multi-move PATTERN (across-then-up) to build a staircase, and count moves and total height by multiplying per-step amounts by the repeat count.

parts.title: Curriculum (Ontario Math 2020, Strand C3)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential, concurrent, and repeating events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: Python Turtle projected (or a web playground); the printed worksheet + a pencil per student. Graph paper helps draw the staircase.

parts.title: Run it (about 30 min)
text: 1. Walk a staircase as a class — across, up, across, up — name the repeating step.
2. Run the range(3) staircase; trace one step, then the repeat.
3. Students do Exercises 1–4 (Ex 4 multiplies the rise), solo or in pairs.
4. Share answers; land the big idea: a loop can repeat a pattern of moves.

parts.title: Answer key (checked by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — 3 steps; 6 forward moves (2 per step × 3).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: counting one forward per step instead of two.
Support: highlight the two forward lines inside the loop before counting.
Extend: ask the height of a 6-step staircase (180).

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The student counts steps and total forwards (Ex 1–2), writes the range for a 4-step staircase (Ex 3), and multiplies the rise to find the total height (Ex 4).
